questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola with Vertex at the Origin Given Another Point
questions.problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(5,5).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(5,5),$ we can substitute $x=5$ and $y=5$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {5}^{2} & =4p(5) \\ 25 & =20p \\ p & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(\frac{5}{4})x \\ {y}^{2} & =5x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola Given a Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14041157/assets/9eb2efa6d60dc4bd1d7915900e60be8a891f824799ed6ada8f2753fa71bb01c6.png)

What is the equation of the parabola shown above?
questions.worked_solution:
From the diagram we see that the arms of the parabola open to the left. The parabola has its vertex at $(-2,2)$ and passes through the point $(6,10).$

The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-2,2),$ we substitute $h=-2$ and $k=2$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(6,10),$ so we can substitute $x=6$ and $y=10$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+2) \\ (10-2)^{2} & =4p(6+2) \\ 64 & =32p \\ p & =2\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-2)^{2} & =4p(x+2) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =4(2)(x+2) \\ (y-2)^{2} & =8(x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that the arms of the parabola open to the right since $p=2$ is positive.

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Equation of a Left or Right-Opening Parabola Given the Vertex and Another Point
questions.problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-3,1)$ and passes through the point $(0,5).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-3,1),$ we substitute $h=-3$ and $k=1$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-1)^{2} & =4p(x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(0,5),$ so we can substitute $x=0$ and $y=5$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-1)^{2} & =4p(x+3) \\ (5-1)^{2} & =4p(0+3) \\ 16 & =12p \\ p & =\frac{4}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-1)^{2} & =4p(x+3) \\ (y-1)^{2} & =4(\frac{4}{3})(x+3) \\ (y-1)^{2} & =\frac{16}{3}(x+3).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(0,0)$ and passes through the point $(-2,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(0,0)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
{y}^{2}=4px.
$$

Since we know the given parabola passes through the point $(-2,-2),$ we can substitute $x=-2$ and $y=-2$ into the standard equation and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ (-2)^{2} & =4p(-2) \\ 4 & =-8p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4px \\ {y}^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{2})x \\ {y}^{2} & =-2x.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the equation of the left-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(2,0)$ and passes through the point $(0,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(2,0),$ we substitute $h=2$ and $k=0$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(0,-2),$ so we can substitute $x=0$ and $y=-2$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ (-2)^{2} & =4p(0-2) \\ 4 & =-8p \\ p & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2} & =4p(x-2) \\ {y}^{2} & =4(-\frac{1}{2})(x-2) \\ {y}^{2} & =-2(x-2).\end{aligned}
$$
